authorities.proposition_supported: Criminal appellate notice: oral notice at trial, or written notice filed and served within fourteen days of judgment or a qualifying timely MAR ruling. District-to-superior appeals use separate statutes.

authorities.proposition_supported: Preservation ordinarily requires a timely specific request and ruling. Jury-instruction objections precede deliberation when opportunity exists. A dismissal motion at the close of all evidence preserves sufficiency regardless of an earlier motion; introducing defense evidence waives denial of the State-close motion. Plain error must be distinctly asserted; its availability requires separate precedent review.

authorities.proposition_supported: Guilty-plea appellate rights are limited, with exceptions including specified sentencing issues, section 15A-979, and denial of plea withdrawal. Subsection (a1) concerns evidentiary support for a nonpresumptive felony minimum; (a2) identifies sentencing legality issues. Certiorari is a separate route, not an automatic appeal.

authorities.proposition_supported: A final suppression denial may be reviewed on appeal from conviction, including conviction on a guilty plea. Reservation, notice, waiver, and other procedural requirements need current primary-opinion review.

authorities.proposition_supported: Superior-court plea discussions may involve charge or sentence concessions and judicial participation. Improper pressure is prohibited. A judge may withdraw advance concurrence when later information is inconsistent with the arrangement.

authorities.proposition_supported: Plea acceptance requires the statutory rights inquiry, informed choice, and factual basis. Personal-address requirements have statutory exceptions for corporations and qualifying misdemeanor appearance waivers. A no-contest plea does not require an admission of guilt.

authorities.proposition_supported: Sentence arrangements must be disclosed. Rejection requires reasons, releases the parties from the agreement, and permits modification and the prescribed continuance; rejection is recorded on the plea transcript. Charge-only arrangements also must be disclosed.
